13894-the-great-adventure-a-play-of-fanc.title: A Play of Fancy in Four Acts
13894-the-great-adventure-a-play-of-fanc.creator: Arnold Bennett
13894-the-great-adventure-a-play-of-fanc.description: A book by Arnold Bennett. At back double doors (ajar) leading to another room. Door, L., leading to hall and front door. TIME.--Evening in August. ALBERT SHAWN is reclining on the sofa, fully dressed, but obviously ill: an overcoat has been drawn over his legs. A conspicuous object is a magnificent light purple dressing-gown thrown across a chair. Enter ILAM CARVE in his shirt sleeves, hurriedly. SHAWN feebly tries to get up. Remember you're a sick man, and forget you're a servant.

arxiv-2001-02078.title: An alternative interpretation of the cosmological vacuum
arxiv-2001-02078.creator: Thomas Schürmann
arxiv-2001-02078.description: Abstract The present contribution aims at obtaining the energy/dark energy fraction of the universe by starting from the Sitter vacuum only and without involving any additional source of energy. To do so, we consider two different standard solutions of the Einstein vacuum equations with positive cosmological constant.

arxiv-2204-07786.title: Approaching sales forecasting using recurrent neural networks and transformers Journal: Expert Systems With Applications
arxiv-2204-07786.creator: Iván Vallés-Pérez, Emilio Soria-Olivas, Marcelino Martínez-Sober, Antonio J. Serrano-López, Juan Gómez-Sanchís, Fernando Mateo
arxiv-2204-07786.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Iván Vallés-Pérez, Emilio Soria-Olivas, Marcelino Martínez-Sober, Antonio J. Serrano-López, Juan Gómez-Sanchís, Fernando Mateo. Accurate and fast demand forecast is one of the hot topics in supply chain for enabling the precise execution of the corresponding downstream processes (inbound and outbound planning, inventory placement, network planning, etc). We develop three alternatives to tackle the problem of forecasting the customer sales at day/store/item level using deep learning techniques and the Corporación Favorita data set, published as part of a Kaggle competition.

arxiv-2302-00111.title: Learning Universal Policies via Text-Guided Video Generation
arxiv-2302-00111.creator: Yilun Du † ‡, Mengjiao Yang * ‡ §, Bo Dai ‡ ¶, Hanjun Dai ‡, Ofir Nachum ‡, Google DeepMind ‡, UC Berkeley §, Georgia Tech ¶, University of Alberta ∥
arxiv-2302-00111.description: Abstract A goal of artificial intelligence is to construct an agent that can solve a wide variety of tasks. Recent progress in text-guided image synthesis has yielded models with an impressive ability to generate complex novel images, exhibiting combinatorial generalization across domains. Motivated by this success, we investigate whether such tools can be used to construct more general-purpose agents.

arxiv-2403-09266.title: Quadratic Riemann-Roch formulas
arxiv-2403-09266.creator: Frédéric Déglise, Jean Fasel
arxiv-2403-09266.description: Abstract Introduction Orientation theory and Riemann-Roch formulas after Grothendieck Starting from an astonishing six pages paper by Quillen [ Qui69 ] , the intrication between formal group laws and homotopy theory has emerged and flourished for more than fifty years.

arxiv-2407-15757.title: Willingness to Pay for an Electricity Connection: A Choice Experiment Among Rural Households and Enterprises in Nigeria
arxiv-2407-15757.creator: Pouya Janghorban, Temilade Sesan, Muhammad-Kabir Salihu, Olayinka Ohunakin, Narges Chinichian
arxiv-2407-15757.description: Abstract Rural electrification initiatives worldwide frequently encounter financial planning challenges due to a lack of reliable market insights. This research delves into the preferences and marginal willingness to pay (mWTP) for upfront electricity connections in rural and peri-urban areas of Nigeria.

arxiv-2503-01366.title: Analogs of the lower and upper central series in skew braces: a survey
arxiv-2503-01366.creator: Cindy (Sin Yi) Tsang
arxiv-2503-01366.description: Abstract A skew brace is a ring-like and group-like algebraic structure that was introduced in the study of set-theoretic solutions to the Yang-Baxter equation. In this survey paper, we shall consider the left series, right series, socle series, and annihilator series of skew braces. They may be regarded as analogs of the lower and upper central series of groups.

arxiv-2507-01285.title: Far From Sight, Far From Mind: Inverse Distance Weighting for Graph Federated Recommendation
arxiv-2507-01285.creator: Aymen Rayane Khouas (✉), Mohamed Reda Bouadjenek, Hakim Hacid, Sunil Aryal
arxiv-2507-01285.description: Abstract Graph federated recommendation systems offer a privacy-preserving alternative to traditional centralized recommendation architectures, which often raise concerns about data security. While federated learning enables personalized recommendations without exposing raw user data, existing aggregation methods overlook the unique properties of user embeddings in this setting.

arxiv-2510-01946.title: Colored Petri Nets are Monoidal Double Functors
arxiv-2510-01946.creator: Jade Master and Joe Moeller
arxiv-2510-01946.description: Abstract . We give a characterization of colored Petri nets as monoidal double functors. Framing colored Petri nets in terms of category theory allows for canonical definitions of various well-known constructions on colored Petri nets. In particular, we show how morphisms of colored Petri nets may be understood as natural transformations.

arxiv-2510-09344.title: WildElder: A Chinese Elderly Speech Dataset from the Wild with Fine-Grained Manual Annotations
arxiv-2510-09344.creator: Hui Wang, Jiaming Zhou, Jiabei He, Haoqin Sun, Yong Qin
arxiv-2510-09344.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Hui Wang, Jiaming Zhou, Jiabei He, Haoqin Sun, Yong Qin. Elderly speech poses unique challenges for automatic processing due to age-related changes such as slower articulation and vocal tremors. Existing Chinese datasets are mostly recorded in controlled environments, limiting their diversity and real-world applicability. To address this gap, we present WildElder, a Mandarin elderly speech corpus collected from online videos and enriched with fine-grained manual annotations, including transcription, speaker age, gender, and accent strength.

arxiv-2601-22315.title: Gaussian Process Bandit Optimization with Machine Learning Predictions and Application to Hypothesis Generation
arxiv-2601-22315.creator: Xin Jennifer Chen, Yunjin Tong
arxiv-2601-22315.description: Abstract Many real-world optimization problems involve an expensive ground-truth oracle (e.g., human evaluation, physical experiments) and a cheap, low-fidelity prediction oracle (e.g., machine learning models, simulations). Meanwhile, abundant offline data (e.g., past experiments and predictions) are often available and can be used to pretrain powerful predictive models, as well as to provide an informative prior.

pmc-10505305.title: The number of erupted teeth as a risk factor for dental caries in eighteen-month-old children: a cross‑sectional study
pmc-10505305.creator: Masatoshi Otsugu, Yusuke Mikasa, Maika Kadono, Taro Matsuoka, Katsura Matsunami, Motomi Nakamura, Yuko Ohno, Takafumi Kato, Kazuhiko Nakano
pmc-10505305.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). BackgroundDental caries is one of the most common chronic diseases worldwide, affecting lifelong as well as children. Therefore, it is important to clarify factors related to early childhood caries (ECC) in a younger population in terms of caries prevention. However, the prevalence of ECC is low in developed countries in the twenty-first century and a large-scale survey is needed to clarify the risk factors.

pmc-10591955.title: LIF signaling regulates outer radial glial to interneuron fate during human cortical development
pmc-10591955.creator: Madeline G. Andrews, Clara Siebert, Li Wang, Matthew L. White, Jayden Ross, Raul Morales, Megan Donnay, Gradi Bamfonga, Tanzila Mukhtar, Arpana Arjun McKinney, Kaila Gemenes, Shaohui Wang, Qiuli Bi, Elizabeth E. Crouch, Neelroop Parikshak, Georgia Panagiotakos, Eric Huang, Aparna Bhaduri, Arnold R.
pmc-10591955.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). SUMMARYRadial glial (RG) development is essential for cerebral cortex growth and organization. In humans, the outer radial glia (oRG) subtype is expanded and gives rise to diverse neurons and glia. However, the mechanisms regulating oRG differentiation are unclear. oRG cells express leukemia-inhibitory factor (LIF) receptors during neurogenesis, and consistent with a role in stem cell self-renewal, LIF perturbation impacts oRG proliferation in cortical tissue and organoids. Surprisingly, LIF treatment also increases the production of inhibitory interneurons (INs) in cortical cultures.

pmc-11387182.title: A ruthenium single atom nanozyme-based antibiotic for the treatment of otitis media caused by Staphylococcus aureus
pmc-11387182.creator: Jie Wang, Rui Gong, Ming Yang, Xi Wu, Ziwei Li, Haibing Huang, Xiyun Yan, Daji Wang
pmc-11387182.description: Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus) infection is a primary cause of otitis media (OM), the most common disease for which children are prescribed antibiotics. However, the abuse of antibiotics has led to a global increase in antimicrobial resistance (AMR). Nanozymes, as promising alternatives to traditional antibiotics, are being extensively utilized to combat AMR.

pmc-11602025.description: The long non-coding RNA (lncRNA), HAR1A is emerging as a putative tumour suppressor. In non-neoplastic brain cells, REST suppresses HAR1A expression. In gliomas REST acts as an oncogene and is a potential therapeutic target. It is therefore conceivable that REST promotes glioma progression by down-regulating HAR1A.

pmc-12391313.title: A benchmark database of ten years of prospective next-day earthquake forecasts in California from the Collaboratory for the Study of Earthquake Predictability
pmc-12391313.creator: Francesco Serafini, José A Bayona, Fabio Silva, William Savran, Samuel Stockman, Philip J Maechling, Maximilian J Werner
pmc-12391313.description: Short-term seismicity forecasting models are increasingly developed and deployed for Operational Earthquake Forecasting (OEF) by government agencies and research institutions worldwide. To ensure their reliability, these forecasts must be rigorously tested against future observations in a fully prospective manner, allowing researchers to quantify model performance and build confidence in their predictive capabilities.
